newsitem.title: USA: ABC Rail says able to consider purchases.
newsitem.headline: ABC Rail says able to consider purchases.

text.p: ABC Rail Corp said Tuesday that recently completed financing enables it to consider acquisition opportunities created by consolidation in the rail supply industry.
Soon after the close of the fiscal second quarter, which ended January 31, ABC closed a $50 million, seven-year balloon bond issue at 9-1/8 percent, the company said.

ABC, which supplies products and equipment to the rail industry, said this bond issue converted intermediate-term debt to long-term debt and eliminated more than $6.0 million in annual principal payments.
ABC Rail said that, as of January 31, its long-term debt to total capitalization ratio was 44 percent, or about the same as at the July 31 fiscal year-end, in spite of heavy capital expenditures.

"In all, our capital expenditures during the first half of 1997 were $13.0 million, compared with $4.8 million during the prior-year period," Donald Grinter, chairman, said in a statement. "This year's spending includes about $7.4 million for Track Products CNC equipment at Chicago Heights, and about $600,000 for our SAP R/3 computer systems project."
He said the new CNC machines should be operational before the end of fiscal 1997 and contribute to profits starting in fiscal 1998.

"The new computer system is a key element of ABC Rail's ongoing re-engineering of our business processes, which will ultimately lend to increased efficiencies and profitability throughout the business," Grinter said.
Earlier, ABC Rail reported earnings for the second quarter ended January 31 of $0.30 a share on 8.8 million shares outstanding, down from $0.33 on 8.2 million shares.

"As we previously announced, the merger-induced slowdown in orders from western Class I (large) railroads and our historical first-half seasonal lull prompted us to accelerate the facility upgrades and trade off a relatively mild, short-term sales setback in exchange for improved productivity and capacity," Grinter said.
